metrics.label: Gas and coal 40+ years old
metrics.notes: Operating gas and coal units built in 1985 or earlier. Old plants are likely to retire or be rebuilt, and their sites already have grid and gas connections. Age is a guess, not an announced retirement.

metrics.label: Realized capacity factor
metrics.notes: How hard all of the county's power plants ran in 2024: actual output divided by the most they could produce. Capped at 1.0 because higher values are reporting errors. Blank for counties with no power plants.

metrics.label: Gas fleet capacity factor
metrics.notes: How hard the county's existing gas plants ran in 2024. Busy plants suggest gas power is needed there. Blank for counties with no gas plants. Capped at 1.0.

metrics.label: Gas gathering pipe
metrics.source_name: Railroad Commission of Texas pipeline map
metrics.notes: Miles of pipe that collects gas from wells. A sign of nearby production (Permian, Eagle Ford, Haynesville), where gas is usually cheapest. Gathering lines carry raw gas and can't feed a plant directly.

metrics.label: Interstate gas pipe
metrics.source_name: Railroad Commission of Texas pipeline map
metrics.notes: Miles of pipe that crosses state lines. These are federally regulated, with published rates and open access. Pipes inside Texas (about three quarters of the mileage) set terms privately.

metrics.label: Large gas pipe (20 in and up)
metrics.source_name: Railroad Commission of Texas pipeline map
metrics.notes: Miles of transmission pipe 20 inches or wider. Diameter stands in for capacity, which isn't published. Large lines are the ones that can usually supply a power plant; small ones mostly serve towns and industry.

metrics.label: Gas transmission pipe
metrics.source_name: Railroad Commission of Texas pipeline map
metrics.notes: Miles of gas transmission pipe in the county. Shows a plant could connect, not that spare gas is available: capacity and pressure aren't public for pipes inside Texas.

metrics.label: Gas pipeline operators
metrics.source_name: Railroad Commission of Texas pipeline map
metrics.notes: Number of companies with at least 1 mile of transmission pipe in the county. More operators means more supply options and a better negotiating position.

metrics.label: Active gas queue
metrics.notes: MW of gas projects waiting to connect in the county: the direct competition for a new gas plant. Fewer is better. Blank where there are none, since most counties have none. Leaves out confidential projects.

metrics.label: Generation trend 2020-2024
metrics.notes: Change in the county's power output from 2020 to 2024. A 10,000 MWh floor is added so counties with no generation don't all tie for the top.

metrics.label: Existing generation capacity
metrics.notes: Operating power plant capacity in the county. A rough sign that transmission lines are nearby; it says nothing about whether those lines have room for more.

metrics.label: Parcels with a land-use code
metrics.notes: Share of parcels that have a state land-use code. Many counties leave it blank (Wharton, Fort Bend and Travis are at 0%).

metrics.label: Industrial and utility land
metrics.source_name: TxGIO StratMap Land Parcels 2025, state land-use codes F2 and J3
metrics.notes: Acres coded as industrial (F2) or electric utility (J3) land. Only shown where at least 80% of parcels have a land-use code, about a third of counties.

metrics.label: Land in large tracts (100+ ac)
metrics.source_name: TxGIO StratMap Land Parcels 2025 (county appraisal districts)
metrics.notes: Share of parcel acres in parcels of 100 acres or more: room for a plant on land with one owner. Blank where the parcel data covers less than 80% or more than 125% of the county.

metrics.label: Landowners per 1,000 rural acres
metrics.source_name: TxGIO StratMap Land Parcels 2025 (county appraisal districts)
metrics.notes: Number of different owners of 5+ acre parcels per 1,000 acres of those parcels: how many landowners a project may have to deal with. The same owner spelled differently counts twice. Blank where parcel data is incomplete.

metrics.label: Parcel coverage of county
metrics.source_name: TxGIO StratMap Land Parcels 2025 and US Census
metrics.notes: Parcel acres divided by the county's Census land area. Close to 1.0 means the parcel data is complete. Harris is 0.40 (partial file); Frio (2.8) and Chambers (1.7) have overlapping parcels. Land scores are blank outside 0.8 to 1.25.

metrics.label: Parcel data month
metrics.notes: Month the county appraisal district's data was collected.

metrics.label: Parcels of 500+ acres
metrics.source_name: TxGIO StratMap Land Parcels 2025 (county appraisal districts)
metrics.notes: Number of single parcels of 500 acres or more: tracts big enough for a plant plus a buffer. Blank where parcel data is incomplete.

metrics.label: LNG export terminals
metrics.source_name: Compiled by hand; Golden Pass status from EIA, April 2026
metrics.notes: LNG export terminals operating or under construction. They compete for pipeline gas but also mean large supply lines are nearby. Status needs checking now and then.

metrics.label: LNG export terminals (names)
metrics.notes: Terminal names and status, for example "Golden Pass LNG (Operating)".

metrics.label: NOx credit price (area median)
metrics.notes: Median price paid for NOx credits in the area, a one-time purchase per ton per year. Blank where the area had no priced trades (San Antonio and El Paso).

metrics.label: NOx credit tons traded (area)
metrics.notes: Tons per year of NOx credits sold in the area, Oct 2024 to Sep 2026. Houston sold 87 in two years; one 100-ton-per-year plant at 1.3 to 1 would need 130.

metrics.label: NOx credit trades (area)
metrics.notes: Number of priced NOx credit trades in the county's ozone area, Oct 2024 to Sep 2026. Credits must come from the same area, so few trades can mean credits are hard to find at any price.

metrics.label: NOx major source threshold
metrics.source_name: Clean Air Act nonattainment permit rules
metrics.notes: A plant emitting this much NOx or more needs a nonattainment permit and must buy offset credits. Only for counties that fail an ozone standard. Elsewhere, plants still need pollution controls but don't buy offsets.

metrics.label: NOx offset cost per ton emitted
metrics.source_name: Calculated: offset ratio x area credit price
metrics.notes: Up-front credit cost for each ton per year of NOx the plant will emit; multiply by the plant's own emissions. 0 where no offsets are needed; blank where the area had no priced trades.

metrics.label: NOx offset ratio
metrics.unit: tons of credit per ton emitted
metrics.source_name: Clean Air Act nonattainment permit rules
metrics.notes: Tons of credits a plant must buy for each ton of NOx it will emit. 0 where no offsets are needed.

metrics.label: Ozone classification
metrics.notes: The county's EPA ozone rating. Houston and Dallas-Fort Worth are Severe under the 2008 standard and Serious under 2015; permits follow the stricter one.

metrics.label: Ozone nonattainment severity
metrics.notes: EPA ozone rating under the stricter of the 2008 and 2015 standards: 0 Attainment, 1 Marginal, 2 Moderate, 3 Serious, 4 Severe, 5 Extreme. A worse rating means a harder, more expensive air permit.

metrics.label: Ozone standards breached
metrics.notes: Each ozone standard the county fails and its rating, for example "2008: Severe 15; 2015: Serious". Only for counties that fail one.

metrics.label: Population density
metrics.source_name: US Census population estimates (2025) and Gazetteer land area (2024)
metrics.notes: Fewer people means fewer neighbors near a plant and usually less local opposition. A rough measure only.

metrics.label: Queue attrition rate
metrics.notes: Not in the score. Share of past projects in the county that dropped out of the queue, pulled toward the statewide rate where there's little history. Counties differ by only about 0.01, so scoring it would turn noise into big differences.

metrics.label: Active interconnection queue
metrics.notes: MW of all projects waiting to connect to the grid in the county. Fewer is better: less competition for the same connection. Leaves out confidential projects ERCOT hasn't published yet.

metrics.label: Capacity retiring by 2030
metrics.notes: Not in the score. EIA lists planned ERCOT retirements through 2030 almost only in Bexar County, so this doesn't separate counties. Plant age (Gas and coal 40+ years old) is used instead.
